domain: Artificial Intelligence / Open Weights / Frontier Compute

slides.title: Open weights. Counted compute.
slides.body: Read the license. Inspect the architecture. Audit the denominator.

slides.title: Open means more than downloadable
slides.body: OSI’s Open Source AI Definition 1.0 requires these components under OSI-approved terms or licenses.

cards.title: 01 · Data information
cards.body: Training-data descriptions, provenance, processing methods, and locations of public and third-party datasets.

cards.title: 02 · Code
cards.body: Complete training and inference source, including processing, filtering, settings, validation, testing, supporting libraries, and architecture.

cards.title: 03 · Parameters
cards.body: Model weights and other configuration settings—not merely access to an endpoint.

slides.title: The rack is the unit
slides.body: NVIDIA’s GB200 NVL72 combines 72 Blackwell GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs in a liquid-cooled rack.
slides.image_direction: Original rack schematic; highlight GPU interconnects and cooling paths.

cards.title: GPU memory
cards.body: 13.4 TB HBM3E; 576 TB/s memory bandwidth.

cards.title: NVLink
cards.body: 130 TB/s bandwidth across the rack-scale interconnect.

slides.title: DeepSeek-V3: the training ledger
slides.body: Reported official training costs assume H800 rental at $2 per GPU hour; prior research and ablations are excluded.

cards.title: Pre-training
cards.body: 2664K H800 GPU hours · $5.328M.

cards.title: Context extension
cards.body: 119K H800 GPU hours · $0.238M.

cards.title: Post-training
cards.body: 5K H800 GPU hours · $0.01M.

cards.title: Total
cards.body: 2788K H800 GPU hours · $5.576M.

slides.title: The download is not the definition
slides.label: ILLUSTRATIVE EXCHANGE

cards.speaker: Reader
cards.body: I can download the weights. Is that enough?

cards.speaker: Editor
cards.body: Not under OSI’s Definition 1.0: data information and derivation code must accompany the parameters.

cards.speaker: Reader
cards.body: Which freedoms should I check?

cards.speaker: Editor
cards.body: Use, study, modify, and share—including use and modification for any purpose.

slides.title: Separate access from operation
slides.body: Editorial framework: evaluate weight access and deployment location independently.

cards.title: Unavailable · Provider-hosted
cards.body: Ask about retention, portability, pricing, and service limits.

cards.title: Available · Provider-hosted
cards.body: Check license rights separately from hosting terms.

cards.title: Unavailable · Self-hosted
cards.body: Inspect appliance restrictions, update control, and audit access.

cards.title: Available · Self-hosted
cards.body: Budget infrastructure; verify modification and redistribution rights.

slides.title: DeepSeek-V3: sparsity, not smallness
slides.body: The architecture separates total model capacity from parameters activated for each token.

cards.title: Capacity
cards.body: 671B total parameters; 37B activated per token.

cards.title: Training
cards.body: 14.8T pre-training tokens; FP8 mixed precision.

cards.title: Context extension
cards.body: Two stages: first 32K, then 128K maximum context length.

slides.title: A training bill is not an R&D bill

cards.title: Misreading
cards.body: The reported $5.576M covers all DeepSeek-V3 development.

cards.title: Correction
cards.body: $5.576M estimates official training at $2 per H800 GPU hour; prior research and ablation experiments are excluded.

cards.title: Editorial rule
cards.body: Attach the accounting boundary to every cost headline.

slides.title: The Compute Review audit grid
slides.body: Before publishing a comparison, require these fields.

cards.title: Access
cards.body: License version; weight availability; training-code availability; data documentation.

cards.title: Architecture
cards.body: Total parameters; active parameters per token; context length in tokens.

cards.title: Compute
cards.body: Accelerator model; accelerator count; GPU hours; numerical precision.

cards.title: Economics
cards.body: Currency; hourly rate; included stages; excluded experiments; measurement date.

slides.headline: Access is not infrastructure
slides.body: “Open weights change who can deploy. They do not erase the compute bill.”

slides.headline: Benchmark before you buy
slides.body: OpenAI reports gpt-oss-120b runs on one 80 GB GPU; gpt-oss-20b needs 16 GB memory.

slides.headline: $5.576M
slides.body: DeepSeek-V3 official training: 2788K H800 GPU-hours at $2 per GPU-hour; excludes prior research and ablation experiments.

slides.headline: Test all three reasoning settings
slides.body: 1. Low → 2. Medium → 3. High: gpt-oss reasoning settings. Measure accuracy, latency, and cost at each.

slides.headline: Read beyond the model name
slides.body: DO distinguish gpt-oss-120b’s 117B total parameters from 5.1B active per token. DON'T treat them as interchangeable.

slides.headline: Demand deployment telemetry
slides.body:
□ Task accuracy (%)
□ p95 latency (ms)
□ Throughput (tokens/s)
□ Peak memory (GB)
□ Cost per successful task ($)
slides.label: Editorial measurement checklist

slides.headline: Inside gpt-oss-120b
slides.body: 36 layers; 117B total parameters; 5.1B active parameters/token; 128 experts; 4 active experts/token; 128k context length.
